title: Second-Order Minimax Risk for Interaction Effects with Budgeted Dyad Observation in Two-Sided Markets
banked_reason: Fresh citation-attested D0.5 math and decision reviews pass; novelty review caps at subfield (paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4), not salvageable within scope; independent main validity agrees. Operator standing decision banks below-field and stops.
proof_attempt_summary: C_A N^(-4/3)+o(N^(-4/3)) for each fixed d>=2, with a legal original-record attainer and all-procedure converse. Five cited leaves were repaired with independently retrieved exact source statements, and fresh math/decision reviews passed; the terminal novelty review and independent main validity agree this is subfield rather than field. Formalization was not launched, so no Lean proof, axiom audit, or substrate promotion is claimed; re-raise only with materially broader scope or practical finite-sample/computational gains.
tldr: For the average four-cell interaction in a finite buyer--seller population with independently balanced endpoint assignments and exactly \(dN\) outcome-blind logged dyads, the minimax risk satisfies \(R_N(d)=16/N-16C_A N^{-4/3}+o(N^{-4/3})\) for every fixed integer \(d\ge2\). A core-and-fill logging law and compatible-core conditional Airy rule attain the expansion from the original record, while an embedded endpoint subclass gives the matching all-procedure converse. The first correction is negative, has normalization \(N^{-4/3}\), coefficient \(-16C_A\), and is independent of the fixed budget. The intended consumer is a prospective balanced experiment on bounded raw financial-link changes.
gap: Unrestricted two-arm second-order minimax theory and the public multiarm rate result leave repeated balanced endpoint labels and exact sparse dyad observation untreated. Two-sided projection theory does not establish a uniform second-order risk bound over the bounded schedule cube.
fill: The local cusp and original-record risk identity isolate that competition. The main open question requires an attaining observation rule, a matching all-procedure converse, and a certified constant computation when necessary.
